title.narrative: Lifesaving Emergency Integrated Nutrition Response in Shalla District

description.narrative: ltpgtThe proposed integrated Nutrition project in Shalla District utilizes an intersectoral approach, integrating Nutrition, Health, Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH), Agriculture, and Cash Assistance to significantly enhance access to emergency preventive and curative nutrition services. The project specifically targets nutritionally vulnerable children under five and mothers/caretakers of children under two.ltbrgtTo ensure high-quality service delivery across the eight targeted Primary Health Care Units (PHCUs) in the Woreda, the project will deploy a team consisting of a Zonal Health and Nutrition Coordinator, a Community-based Management of Acute Malnutrition (CMAM) officer, a health officer, a nutrition officer, a livelihood officer, a WASH officer, and a driver. This team will focus on Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) management, micronutrient supplementation, and Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF) practices, integrating all project components effectively on the ground.ltbrgtBuilding on existing initiatives in Oromia, the project will target operational Woreda with established programs and partnerships. Key components include Emergency Nutrition Supports such as regular nutritional screening, SAM management, micronutrient supplementation, deworming, and Infant and Young Child Feeding-E (IYCF-E). It will also ensure the availability of safe water and handwashing facilities.ltbrgtWASH elements are critical to the project’s success. At the household level, WASH Non-Food Items (NFIs) such as clean water containers (Jerry cans), soap, and sanitation supplies will be distributed. Health facilities will receive WASH infrastructure support to maintain hygiene and sanitation standards. The project will emphasize hygiene and sanitation promotion through community engagement and capacity-building training to improve local practices.ltbrgtIn the agricultural sector, the project will provide high-nutrition items including egg-laying chickens, fruits, and cereals to enhance food security and nutritional intake. Cash support will also be provided to assist recovery from SAM following discharge from Stabilization Centers (SCs).ltbrgtA robust Post-Distribution Monitoring (PDM) system will be employed to track and evaluate the distribution of all items and services, ensuring that the needs of target populations are effectively met.ltbrgtWorld Vision Ethiopia (WVE) will collaborate closely with the Regional Health Bureau (RHB), the nutrition cluster, the health cluster, WASH cluster, Agriculture and Cash cluster, Oromia Water Bureau, Oromia Agriculture Bureau, Oromia Water Bureau, and local partner, called Hope Integrated Social Development Organization (HISD). This collaboration will focus on strengthening existing health facilities and identifying suitable locations for new stabilization centers to manage SAM cases with medical complications. The project will foster a collaborative environment with the RHB and Woreda health offices, engaging the health system workforce at all levels. Capacity-building efforts will encompass CMAM, IYCF-E, micronutrient supplementation, and outreach services.ltbrgtTimely delivery of essential nutrition materials and supplies—including therapeutic supplies, nutrition registers/booklets, Outpatient Therapeutic Program (OTP) cards, Information, Education, and Communication/Behavior Change Communication (IEC/BCC) materials, anthropometric equipment, and stationery—will be ensured. All distributions and activities will adhere to the health tier system and other clusters’ standards in the targeted Woreda.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgt
